notes: Epson uses the same E-/W-/I- code scheme across its ink tank models with screens.

guides.title: Lines missing in the nozzle check

steps.title: Check the basics
steps.text: Ink tanks above the lower line, no air gaps in the tubes, plain paper loaded, no error lights.

steps.title: Print a nozzle check
steps.text: {nozzle_check} In this app: Maintenance → Nozzle check pattern.

steps.title: Only one colour affected?
steps.text: Print 2–3 solid pages of that colour first (see 'Purge a single colour'). It uses only that ink and nothing goes to the waste pads.

steps.title: Clean once
steps.text: {head_cleaning} Then print another nozzle check.

steps.title: Up to three cleanings
steps.text: If it improves, repeat up to three times in total, checking after each.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Still gaps after three cleanings: switch off and wait at least 12 hours (or overnight). Soaking the cap meanwhile helps (see 'Soak the capping station').

steps.title: Power cleaning, once
steps.text: Only if most lines are still missing: {power_cleaning}

steps.title: Stop
steps.text: No improvement after a power cleaning and another 12-hour rest: the head may be damaged or a tube may be blocked; contact a service centre.

warnings: Every cleaning sends ink to the waste pads; back-to-back cleanings fill them fast.
Power cleaning needs every tank at least one-third full, or it can damage the printer.
Never switch off or open the cover during a cleaning.
tips: A pattern that gets better each time is worth one more try; one that never changes needs rest, not cleaning.

guides.title: Purge a single colour (save ink)

steps.title: Why
steps.text: Cleaning always pulls ink from every colour, because one cap covers the whole head. Printing a solid page fires only that colour's nozzles.

steps.title: Make the page
steps.text: A page filled with pure colour: yellow RGB 255,255,0 · cyan 0,255,255 · magenta 255,0,255 · black 0,0,0. Paint or Word is enough.

steps.title: Print 2–3 pages
steps.text: Through the normal Epson driver, plain paper, standard quality, a few minutes apart.

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Print a nozzle check. Better but gappy: repeat once. Unchanged: soak the cap, then try again.

tips: Works best when the colour is thin or broken, not completely missing.
If a colour is missing entirely right after a refill or tube work, suspect air in the tube instead.

guides.title: Soak the capping station (fluid under the head)

steps.title: Get the head off the cap
steps.text: Lift the scanner unit. Start a nozzle check or cleaning; as soon as the head moves left off its parking spot, pull the power cable from the wall. Don't use the power button: it parks the head first.

steps.title: Find the cap and wiper
steps.text: On the right, where the head rests: a small rectangular rubber cap and a thin rubber blade next to it. Don't touch the clear encoder strip or the white ribbon cable.

steps.title: Clean the cap rim and wiper
steps.text: Lint-free swab or cotton bud lightly dampened with distilled water. Dried ink on the rim stops the cap from sealing.

steps.title: Fill the cap
steps.text: Distilled water or printhead cleaning fluid, a few drops, level with the rim, not overflowing.

steps.title: Park the head on the wet cap
steps.text: Slide the head gently by hand back to the right until it sits in its parking position. Don't force it.

steps.title: Let it soak
steps.text: Leave it unplugged at least 4 hours, ideally overnight. This uses no ink.

steps.title: Plug in and check
steps.text: Switch on and print a nozzle check; judge the second or third pattern, not the first. Better but gappy: purge that colour. Unchanged: soak once more before cleaning.

warnings: Never touch the nozzle plate under the head.
No alcohol or household cleaners: they can harden the rubber.
Don't slide the head sideways while it sits on the wet cap.
tips: The same procedure works on all Epson ink tank printers whose head parks on the right.

guides.title: Move the print head out of the way

steps.title: Why there's no button
steps.text: Epson printers only move the head themselves; there is no safe 'move head' command.

steps.title: Unplug mid-movement
steps.text: Start a nozzle check or cleaning and pull the power cable as the head moves left. Unplugged, the head slides by hand with light pressure.

steps.title: Put it back
steps.text: Slide it to the right until it parks over the cap, or just switch on: the printer homes it.

warnings: Only unplug for maintenance; normally always switch off with the power button so the head gets capped.

guides.title: A colour is completely missing after a refill

steps.title: Look at the tank and tube
steps.text: Tank above the lower line? Visible air gaps in that colour's tube?

steps.title: Refill if low
steps.text: A tank below the lower line lets air into the system.

steps.title: One ink charge
steps.text: Air in the tube needs an ink charge (or one power cleaning), not repeated normal cleanings. Run it once, then rest and print a nozzle check.

warnings: An ink charge uses a lot of ink and fills the waste pads quickly.

guides.title: Waste ink pad full ('service required')

steps.title: Confirm it
steps.text: Open Waste ink pads in this app: a counter near or above 100% confirms it.

steps.title: Deal with the ink
steps.text: The counter is an estimate, but the pads really do hold the ink. Replace or wash the pads, or fit an external waste ink tank (a tube from the pad outlet to a bottle).

steps.title: Back up
steps.text: EEPROM → Full backup before changing anything.

steps.title: Reset
steps.text: Waste ink pads → Reset counters. The app backs up the cells, writes and verifies them.

steps.title: Power-cycle
steps.text: Switch the printer off and on to clear the error.

warnings: Resetting without servicing the pads can let ink leak out of the printer.
tips: Models with a user-replaceable maintenance box (e.g. L8050/L18050): replace the box instead.

guides.title: Ink and paper lights on together after power-on

steps.title: Clear it
steps.text: Press the copy (or Stop) button.

steps.title: Check the head
steps.text: Print a nozzle check: the head may not have been capped and could have dried.

steps.title: Prevent it
steps.text: Always switch off with the power button and wait for the light to go out before unplugging.

steps.title: Cancel the job
steps.text: Cancel printing from the computer or with Stop.

steps.title: Rear feed
steps.text: Gently pull jammed paper out of the rear feed slot.

steps.title: Inside
steps.text: Open the front cover (or scanner unit) and remove paper and torn pieces. Don't touch the parts Epson marks.

steps.title: Clear the error
steps.text: Close the cover and press the copy/Stop button.

guides.title: White or dark lines across prints

steps.title: Nozzle check first
steps.text: Gaps in the pattern → follow 'Lines missing in the nozzle check'.

steps.title: Paper settings
steps.text: Paper type in the driver must match the paper; load it printable side up.

steps.title: Quality
steps.text: Turn off high-speed / bidirectional printing; use Standard or High quality.

steps.title: Alignment
steps.text: Run Print Head Alignment from the driver's Maintenance tab.

steps.title: Ink
steps.text: Refill low tanks.

guides.title: Noise and flashing power light after filling ink
symptoms: power light flashing for a long time

steps.title: It's normal
steps.text: Initial ink charging takes about 20 minutes with noise; the power light stops flashing when done.

steps.title: Don't interrupt
steps.text: Switching off early can charge the head badly and waste ink later.

steps.title: Stuck?
steps.text: No movement or noise for 20 minutes and still not finished: switch off and on and check again.

steps.title: Print something weekly
steps.text: A small colour page every week keeps every nozzle wet.

steps.title: Keep tanks topped up
steps.text: Never run below the lower line.

steps.title: Switch off properly
steps.text: Use the power button so the head gets capped; avoid power strips switched off while on.

steps.title: Before a long break
steps.text: Print a nozzle check before leaving, and use the soak method if it comes back clogged.

guides.title: Printer stops mid-print with a high-pitched whine

steps.title: Release it
steps.text: Maintenance → Release stuck job sends a form feed that finishes the open page.

steps.title: Or power-cycle
steps.text: Switch the printer off and on.

steps.title: Why
steps.text: A job that never sends its end-of-page leaves the printer waiting for more data.

steps.title: Wait
steps.text: Windows or Epson's status monitor is using the port, usually for a print job. The app reconnects by itself.

steps.title: Check the queue
steps.text: Cancel stuck jobs in the Windows print queue.

steps.title: Power
steps.text: Make sure the printer is on and not asleep.

steps.title: Read the reason
steps.text: The app checks the printer status first and names the blocker: error, not idle, cleaning disabled for a colour, ink low.

steps.title: Fallback
steps.text: When nothing blocks it, the app sends the Epson-driver cleaning directly instead and confirms it by the waste counter rising.

steps.title: Rate limits
steps.text: Some firmwares refuse strong/power cleaning shortly after another one; wait a while.

guides.title: Counter reset refused by the printer (:NA;)

steps.title: Use USB
steps.text: Many recent firmwares block EEPROM access over the network.

steps.title: Check the model
steps.text: A wrong model selection uses the wrong key; let the app auto-detect.

steps.title: Temporary reset
steps.text: Waste ink pads → Temporary reset (rw) works on some locked firmwares; the effect may not be permanent.
